title: Spread in One Number
objective: After this level you can explain the standard deviation in plain words as the typical distance of values from the average.
summary: The standard deviation is a typical distance of values from the mean, built from every value: small when values bunch together, large when they scatter.

cards.headline: The range listens to two values. Can one number listen to all of them?
cards.body: Yes, and you have probably seen its name in a report: the standard deviation. Karl Pearson gave it that name. You will not calculate it here; you just need to know what it is telling you.

cards.headline: How far from the average, typically
cards.body: The standard deviation measures how far values sit from their mean. Think of it as a typical distance from the average. Unlike the range, it takes every value into account, asking how close each one is to the mean. It also comes in the same units as the data: measure in minutes, and it comes out in minutes.

cards.headline: Small means tight, big means scattered
cards.body: Take two sets that both have a mean of 6. In one, the values run from 4 to 8, mostly 5s, 6s and 7s; its standard deviation is about 1. In the other, they run from 1 to 11, and it is about 3. Same center, three times the typical distance. If every value were identical, the standard deviation would be zero.

cards.fact: Karl Pearson named it the standard deviation in 1893.
cards.context: He used the term in a lecture and put it in print in 1894, replacing older names such as "mean error". The idea itself was already nearly a century old. What stuck was the name, and now a report can say in one number how spread out its data are.

cards.headline: Standard deviation: typical distance
learned: SD: typical distance from the mean
Small SD: tight; big SD: scattered

questions.prompt: In plain words, what does the standard deviation measure?

options.label: The gap between the largest and smallest values
How many of the values are above the mean
options.rationale: It measures distance from the mean, not a count.

options.label: The most common distance between two values
options.rationale: It is about distance from the mean, not between pairs.

options.label: How far values typically sit from the mean

questions.explanation: The standard deviation is a typical distance of the values from their mean.

questions.prompt: Match each set of values with its standard deviation.
questions.explanation: The set running from 4 to 8 has a standard deviation of about 1, the set running from 1 to 11 about 3, and a set of identical values zero.

questions.prompt: Why can the standard deviation give a fuller picture than the range?

options.label: It uses every value, not just the two extremes
It is always a smaller number than the range is
options.rationale: Size is not the point; which values it uses is.

options.label: It ignores outliers completely
options.rationale: It uses every value, outliers included.

options.label: It only works for test scores
options.rationale: It works for any numbers, in their own units.

questions.explanation: The range uses only the largest and smallest values; the standard deviation asks how close every value is to the mean.
